name: Saint Francis de Sales
history: A Savoyard nobleman who gave up a career in law to become a priest, and won much of the Chablais back to the Catholic faith by patient preaching and leaflets slipped under doors. As bishop of Geneva he wrote the Introduction to the Devout Life, teaching that holiness is for everyone in every state of life. He is a Doctor of the Church and patron of writers and journalists.
life: Born at the château of Sales in 1567, Francis studied in Paris and at Padua, where he took a doctorate in law. As a student in Paris he passed through a terrible fear that he was damned, and was freed from it by an act of pure trust before a statue of Our Lady. Against his father’s wishes he was ordained in 1593 and volunteered for the Chablais, south of Lake Geneva, which had become Calvinist. When people would not come to hear him, he wrote out his arguments and had them copied and pushed under doors. Within a few years most of the region had returned to the Church. Named bishop of Geneva in 1602, he lived at Annecy, since Geneva was closed to him. With Saint Jane Frances de Chantal he founded the Visitation nuns. His letters of direction and his Treatise on the Love of God are marked by gentleness and good sense. He died at Lyon in 1622.
prayerTo: Saint Francis de Sales, gentle shepherd and wise guide, you taught that the love of God can flourish in every kitchen, office and home. Pray for me, that I may be patient with others and with myself, do ordinary things with great love, and grow in devotion without anxiety. Pray for all who write and speak in public. Amen.
penance: Practise his gentleness: hold back one sharp word today, and be as patient with your own faults as you would be with a friend’s.
meditation: Francis taught that devotion belongs not only in the cloister but in the barracks, the shop, the court and the household. What would devotion look like in your own ordinary day?
